back: People of about the same age and status who interact closely, such as classmates, friends or teammates.
The influence of peers on one another to behave, dress or think in a certain way; it can be positive or negative.
Values and habits a school teaches without timetabling them: punctuality, discipline, obedience, teamwork, respect for authority.
A small, closed group of friends that keeps others out and expects members to follow its ways.
Neatness, equality (rich and poor look alike) and a sense of belonging to the school.

front: Give two examples of positive peer pressure.
back: Encouraging friends to study; joining a sports team, club or volunteer project together.

front: Give two examples of negative peer pressure.
back: Pressure to use alcohol or drugs; pressure to bunk lessons, bully others or take sexual risks.

front: How can a young person resist negative peer pressure?
back: Think of the consequences, say no clearly, suggest an alternative, choose supportive friends and talk to a trusted adult.

front: Formal or informal agent: the school? peers?
back: The school is formal (rules, curriculum, trained staff); peers are informal (unwritten group norms).
